description.narrative:
Since establishment, the University of Hargeisa has trained 900 youth on employability, entrepreneurship, and career coaching and connected them to markets for job or internship placement. Indeed, UOH exceeded the expectations set at the beginning. However, the Work in Progress project was designed to support the center in its first three years (2020–2022), both financially and operationally,through yearly MoUs between Oxfam and the University of Hargeisa. The center has meaningfully contributed to young people’s employment and livelihood improvements. The center matches the ambitions and career goals of young people with the needs and opportunities in the labour market.
The need to continue supporting this center has become apparent, and recent meetings between the University of Hargeisa and Oxfam Management, led by the CD, agreed to extend the support for 2023 and possibly 2024. Based on the previous learnings, the center will advance its service to youth by supporting motivated young people who lack access to decent work and opportunities through skills training, on-the-job-support, and career coaching. The primary goal of core skills training in the coming years will be to help young people gain a better understanding of their own skills and interests so that they can make an informed decision about whether to pursue a career as an entrepreneur or seek employment. Ultimately, to offer support to gain employment through internships and decent job placement. The training will encompass two main parts, as explained below.
• Employability: The employability will teach participants the relevant soft and hard skills that bridge the gap between their education and the needs of employers. After the training phase, young people transition to an internship or job placement phase that provides them with relevant work experience and helps them develop their professional network. During this track they will get access to one-on-one mentoring and coaching.
• Entrepreneurship: The entrepreneurship will focus more on the development of a business idea in line with the participant’s aspirations and skills. The business ideas with the biggest potential will linked to financial institutions for financing to make their ideas become a reality.
The following results are expected in the (2023).
• Train and coach 100 youth (50% female) on core life skills and entrepreneurship • Place 100 youth (50% female) into internship and decent jobs • Design and pilot ways of sustaining the center operations beyond Oxfam support. Sustainability strategy is expected in early 2024.

participating-org.narrative: The project has no gender capacity building plans, the partner is the University of Hargeisa and they have been implementing access to justice programing with different aid donors and agencies . UOH aspires to become a leading national center ofeducational excellence that meets the nation’s immediate and long-term goals for education and human development. Oxfam has established the Ignite Career Hub at the University of Hargeisa, funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs as part of the LEAD Programme, to address the challenge of youth unemployment in Somaliland. The center provides young people with 21st century skills and links them with job opportunities to help them enter the job market. The University of Hargeisa was selected as thehost of the career center, based on its status as a state university, ownership of premises, and capacity to run and sustain the center's operations
